sections.heading: Gain curve steepness
sections.text: CLLC has a symmetric tank (series L and C on both sides) with a steep gain curve near resonance. If overshoot occurs, move the operating point to the inductive side (f > f_r) where the gain is flatter. The gain curve nonlinearity is worse than LLC near resonance.

sections.heading: Bidirectional mode switching
sections.text: CLLC is designed for bidirectional power flow. If settling is slow during direction reversal, the frequency must sweep through the resonant point. Ensure the control can handle the zero-crossing of power without losing ZVS on both sides.

sections.heading: Light-load flat gain
sections.text: Like LLC, the CLLC gain curve flattens at light load. If regulation fails at light load, consider burst mode or a wider frequency range. The symmetric tank means both sides have the same resonance — the gain curve shape is identical in both directions.

sections.heading: Tank redesign
sections.text: If the CLLC cannot meet specs, the symmetric tank may need asymmetric redesign — different L_r/C_r values on primary and secondary. This breaks the symmetry but allows optimizing for a specific power direction.
